text: Somewhere off the edge of the map, there is an island with one lighthouse, one keeper, and a lamp that has not missed a single night in thirty years.
Until now.
This is the lighthouse. Every night its lamp turns, and every ship that passes steers by it.
A cliff path runs from the lighthouse past the keeper’s cottage, and down to the village.
The village. Two hundred people, one post office, and no secrets. Or so they think.
The harbour, where the boats come in and the gossip goes out.
And the north rocks. Where ships go when the light fails.
Gus has kept this lamp for thirty years. He is sixty, stubborn and kind, and he has never once let it go dark.
He talks to his cat. She does not talk back. Mostly.
Mabel is that cat. She sleeps nineteen hours a day, and in the other five she notices everything.
If Mabel suddenly sits down, pay attention. She only does that for two things. Fish, and fear.
Pip is a gull, and a show-off. From up there he sees every boat, every footprint, and every fib on the island.
Rollo is a mouse. Mostly hungry, sometimes brave, and small enough to get into places nobody else can.
Old Wren runs the post office. She has run it for fifty years, and she knows every old story this island would rather forget.
Dunn is the harbour master. He runs this harbour by the book, and he does not trust Gus. Not one bit.
And Marlo, twenty-two, pilots the ferry to the mainland. Nobody on the council listens to her. They should.
And then there is someone nobody on the island has met. Someone in a yellow coat, who comes up out of the sea at night.
Who she is, and what she wants, is the mystery.
Every day, two short pieces of the story. Every Sunday, the whole chapter, with scenes you have not seen.
Every clue is on screen before it matters. When the story says pause, pause. See if you can solve it before Gus does.
It starts tonight. At twelve minutes past three.
When the lamp goes dark.
